competitors.name: Baseten
competitors.description: Serverless GPU inference for custom/open-weight models; strong presence among AI-native startups (OpenEvidence, Mercor, Abridge, Clay, and others serve on Baseten).

competitors.name: Fireworks AI
competitors.description: Fast inference for open and fine-tuned models, with a fireworks-native serving stack; customers include Cursor, Perplexity, Sourcegraph, Cresta.

competitors.name: Together AI
competitors.description: GPU cloud + inference platform for open-weight and fine-tuned models; also sells training/fine-tuning; customers include Decagon, Jasper, Upstage, Arcee AI.

competitors.name: Seldon
competitors.description: Kubernetes-native model deployment and monitoring platform (Seldon Core), positioned for enterprise MLOps rather than a hosted-inference marketplace.

competitors.name: Modal
competitors.description: Serverless GPU compute platform for running arbitrary Python/ML workloads, popular for real-time inference, fine-tuning, and agentic workloads; customers include Runway, Suno, Hume AI, Cognition.

competitors.name: Anyscale
competitors.description: Commercial platform built on Ray for distributed training and inference at scale; positions around scaling AI workloads across large GPU clusters.

competitors.name: NVIDIA Dynamo
competitors.description: NVIDIA’s open-source, disaggregated-serving inference framework for large-scale LLM deployment across GPU fleets — a direct architectural competitor to MAX at the framework layer.

competitors.name: Google Cloud Vertex AI
competitors.description: GCP’s managed ML platform, including Model Garden and endpoints for serving first-party (Gemini) and third-party/open models.

competitors.name: AWS SageMaker
competitors.description: AWS’s managed ML platform, including SageMaker Inference (real-time, serverless, and async endpoints) and Bedrock for hosted foundation models.
